title.narrative: Land for Youth: Innovate, Secure, Thrive

description.narrative:
Project Goal <(>&<)> Objectives: To empower youth with the knowledge, tools, and networks needed to secure land rights and participate in land governance.
Specific Objectives: 1. Enhance youth awareness of land rights through digital tools, storytelling, and legal training. 2. Facilitate access to land for young farmers by establishing a "Youth Land Bank" that connects landowners with youth agripreneurs. 3. Promote youth participation in land policy dialogues to influence pro-youth land reforms. 4. Support innovative land tenure models (e.g., land-sharing, cooperatives, community-led leasing systems).
Key Activities": A. Youth Land Rights Digital Hub <(>&<)> Training: Develop a mobile-friendly digital platform to provide free resources on land policies, legal rights, and step-by-step guides for youth to access land. Conduct legal literacy workshops for 200+ youth and women on land governance, land tenure security, and negotiation skills. B. "Youth Land Bank" Initiative: Create an online and community-based system where landowners (individuals, government, or private entities) can list available land for youth farmers. Facilitate land-sharing agreements between young agripreneurs and landowners through legal and financial advisory support. C. Storytelling <(>&<)> Advocacy: "My Land, My Future" Campaign: Document real stories of young people and women who successfully accessed land, using video, social media, and community forums. Organize policy dialogues and media engagements where youth present their challenges and recommendations to policymakers. Publish a "Youth Land Rights Report" with case studies and policy recommendations to drive change.
Expected Outcomes <(>&<)> Impact - At least 200 youth and women trained on land rights, tenure security, and advocacy. - 50+ youth agripreneurs connected to landowners through the "Youth Land Bank." - Increased youth participation in land policy discussions at local and national levels. - Greater public awareness through digital storytelling, influencing land governance debates.
Sustainability <(>&<)> Scalability: The digital platform will serve as a long-term resource hub beyond the project timeline. The Youth Land Bank model can be replicated in other regions and scaled through partnerships. The advocacy campaign will continue influencing land policies and ensuring youth inclusion in governance.

participating-org.narrative:
YILAA is international NGO.
We value the potential of young people for land governance; create the synergy of action between youthassociations to become an international Youth network for the promotion and protection of the rights of young people andwomen; helpyoung people identify and benefit from opportunities relating to state projects and support training and research for young people in the land sector.
YILAA is governed by a Board of Directors consisting of nine (9) members, responsible for providing strategic direction and oversight. The organization operates as an International Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) with official legal registration in Tanzania, adhering to the Law of July 1st, 1901.
With an active membership of 300 individuals, YILAA integrates external knowledge into African land governance frameworks, ensuring that youth perspectives are prioritized in agricultural development and climate policies.
YILAA defines marginalization as the exclusion of youth, women, and rural communities from land access and decision-making. To address this, we actively advocate for land rights, provide capacity-building programs, and engage in multi-stakeholder dialogues to ensure inclusion.
Our governance reflects this commitment: - Board of Directors (9 members) includes youth, women, and diverse community leaders. - Staff <(>&<)> Membership (300+ individuals) prioritize young professionals and marginalized groups. - Youth Leadership is central, ensuring young voices shape land policies.
By integrating marginalized groups into both decision-making and implementation, YILAA fosters inclusive land governance across Africa.
Youth Initiative for Land in Africa
